{{Short description|Theoretical physicist}}
'''Martin Roček''' is an American physicist who is a distinguished [[professor]] of [[theoretical physics]] at the [[State University of New York at Stony Brook]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Martin Rocek {{!}} Department of Physics and Astronomy |url=https://www.stonybrook.edu/commcms/physics/people/_profiles/rocekm.php |access-date=2025-10-07 |website=www.stonybrook.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Faculty (alphabetical) {{!}} Department of Physics and Astronomy |url=https://www.stonybrook.edu/commcms/physics/people/faculty/facultyabc.php |access-date=2025-10-07 |website=www.stonybrook.edu |language=en}}</ref> and a member of the [[C. N. Yang Institute for Theoretical Physics]]. He received A.B. and Ph.D. degrees from [[Harvard University]], supervised for his Ph.D. by [[Tai Tsun Wu]] in 1979.<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Ricek |first=Martin |title=Aspects of Spontaneous Symmetry Breakdown of Supersymmetry. |date=1979 |publisher=Harvard University |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=7Dw2wEIAAAAJ&cstart=100&pagesize=100&sortby=pubdate&citation_for_view=7Dw2wEIAAAAJ:BqipwSGYUEgC}}</ref> He did post-doctoral research at the [[University of Cambridge]] and [[Caltech]] before becoming a professor at [[Stony Brook University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Martin Roček {{!}} Science Museum Group Collection |url=https://collection.sciencemuseumgroup.org.uk/people/cp169690/martin-rocek |access-date=2025-10-07 |website=collection.sciencemuseumgroup.org.uk |language=en}}</ref>

He was one of the co-inventors of [[hyperkähler quotient]]s, a hyperkahler analogue of [[Marsden–Weinstein reduction]] and the structure of [[Bihermitian manifold]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hitchin |first=N. J. |author-link=Nigel Hitchin |last2=Karlhede |first2=A. |last3=Lindström |first3=U. |last4=Roček |first4=M. |date=December 1987 |title=Hyperkähler metrics and supersymmetry |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF01214418 |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |language=en |volume=108 |issue=4 |pages=535–589 |doi=10.1007/BF01214418 |issn=0010-3616|url-access=subscription }}</ref>  His research interests include [[supersymmetry]], [[string theory]] and applications of [[generalized complex geometry]]. With [[Sylvester James Gates|S. J. Gates]], [[Marcus Grisaru|M. T. Grisaru]], and [[Warren Siegel|W. Siegel]], Rocek coauthored ''Superspace, or One thousand and one lessons in supersymmetry'' (1984), the first comprehensive book on supersymmetry.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Gates |first1=S. J. Jr. |last2=Grisaru |first2=M. T. |last3=Rocek |first3=M. |last4=Siegel |first4=W. |title=Superspace or One thousand and one lessons in supersymmetry |date=1983 |publisher=Benjamin-Cummings |isbn=0-8053-3160-3}}
:See also {{cite arXiv |last1=Gates |first1=S. J. Jr. |last2=Grisaru |first2=M. T. |last3=Rocek |first3=M. |last4=Siegel |first4=W. |title=Superspace, or One thousand and one lessons in supersymmetry |date=2001 |eprint=hep-th/0108200 }}</ref> He has also contributed extensively to supersymmetry and geometry.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Geometrical Aspects of Supersymmetry: October 22 – 26, 2018 – SCGP |url=https://scgp.stonybrook.edu/archives/24606 |access-date=2025-10-07 |website=scgp.stonybrook.edu}}</ref>

He is the local coordinator of the annual Simons Workshop in Mathematics and Physics<ref>{{Cite web |title=About Martin Rocek |url=http://insti.physics.sunysb.edu/~rocek/plan.html |access-date=2025-10-07 |website=insti.physics.sunysb.edu}}</ref> jointly hosted by Yang Institute for Theoretical Physics and the Department of Mathematics of the Stony Brook University.

In 1991 he received a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Guggenheim Fellowships: Supporting Artists, Scholars, & Scientists |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/martin-rocek |access-date=2025-10-07 |website=www.gf.org}}</ref> In 2017 he received a Neuron Prize for lifelong contributions to science.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Neuron awards in physics |url=https://www.nadaceneuron.cz/en/person/fyzika |access-date=2025-10-07 |website=Nadace Neuron |language=en}}</ref> In 2022 he was appointed as a distinguished professor of physics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Awards by Faculty {{!}} Department of Physics and Astronomy |url=https://www.stonybrook.edu/commcms/physics/about/awards_and_prizes/awardsf.php |access-date=2025-10-07 |website=www.stonybrook.edu |language=en}}</ref>
